title: Rename policy authority and preview parity
summary: Rename preview and production naming now share a versioned, fingerprinted cleaning policy; PowerShell TV naming consumes the saved TV filter settings and the internal preview protocol supports v2 with v1 compatibility.
reason: Saved custom rename terms and disabled categories could be honored by Python while the PowerShell preview or production TV naming used hardcoded defaults, making preview/apply and Queue-adjacent destination naming disagree.
behavior_before: Python requests carried six loose filter fields, the standalone PowerShell preview accepted only naming_preview_request.v1, TV production naming ignored the three RenameTV filter settings, and all-enabled Python shortcuts could skip custom category terms.
behavior_after: Python normalizes rename_cleaning_policy.v1 with a deterministic SHA-256 fingerprint, sends naming_preview_request.v2, validates naming_preview.v2 policy evidence, and binds apply fingerprints to the policy. PowerShell applies only the six allowlisted settings, returns parsed identity evidence, preserves v1 defaults, and production TV cleaning honors configured options, terms, and global TV remove terms.
tests_added: Python rename policy schema/fingerprint determinism and policy-bound apply fingerprint coverage
Python naming preview v2 request, v1/v2 response compatibility, mismatch rejection, policy propagation, and real PowerShell subprocess coverage
PowerShell TV custom-term, disabled-category, custom negative-term, v1 compatibility, v2 policy, and parsed-identity coverage
manual_validation: RED: focused Python tests failed for the missing policy contract, v2 protocol, planner propagation, custom-term fast paths, and policy-bound preview fingerprint.
RED: Invoke-NamingSupportChecks failed because TV production naming ignored the configured MoonSource term and later because preview still returned v1.
GREEN: 65 focused rename/config/Local API tests passed, including the real Python-to-PowerShell preview subprocess.
GREEN: Invoke-NamingSupportChecks, Invoke-ConfigKeyRegistryChecks, and Invoke-RuntimeConfigResolutionChecks passed.
GREEN: WebView Rename readiness and browser smokes passed.
GREEN: targeted Ruff and git diff --check passed.
rollback_plan: Revert the v2 preview transport, policy helpers, TV filter readers, policy-bound fingerprint field, and regression tests together. This packet changes filename/config planning only and does not touch source media or runtime state.
notes: Python impact: internal rename policy dictionaries now expose a versioned nested contract plus compatibility aliases; no public Local API route or persisted config key changed. PowerShell v1 preview behavior remains available for older callers. No commit was created.
